statusText: Green - all 24 published hours fall inside the CME weekend halt, holding Tail at the floor of a closed venue while Saudi confirmation of an intercepted Riyadh missile firms the weekend's geopolitical file without opening an infrastructure channel
recommendation: Mapped policy state: EA_ON. Tail of 4 sits far below the 25% block threshold and no danger window is identified, because every published hour falls inside the weekend futures halt and no live NQ price path exists to assess. Existing-position management and emergency protection are unaffected by this mapping.
headline: Saudi Arabia confirms it intercepted a Houthi ballistic missile over Riyadh with no damage reported, while Hormuz throughput runs at a six-month high across a fully halted weekend
body: Every hour published here falls inside the CME weekend halt. Cash equities closed at 20:00Z Friday, the E-mini printed last at 20:59:59Z at 29,917.25 - up 0.59% from a 29,743.00 previous close but 76 points below its 29,993.25 session high, so the final observed futures mark was not a session extreme - and equity futures do not reopen until 22:00Z Sunday, one hour after the last slot in this window. No published hour contains a tradable tape. Friday's marks were re-verified at primary sources for this run: the cash Nasdaq-100 settled 29,644.17, up 197.17 points or 0.67% from 29,447.00, finishing 3.63 points under the top of a 29,371.89-29,647.80 range and about 3.6% below its 30,762.20 fifty-two-week high. VIX settled 14.81, down 4.08%, at the low of a 14.80-15.63 range. The Fed H.15 release shows the 10-year at 4.94% and the 2-year at 4.67% for 17 September, both easing from 5.01% and 4.74% on 16 September, while the effective federal funds rate stepped to 3.88% after the FOMC raised the target range to 3.75-4.00% on 16 September. WTI settled 100.30, down 1.58%, and Brent 103.87, down 0.91%, with Friday's decline attributed to easing concern over the Saudi East-West pipeline disruption. The material change since the previous published hour is that the Middle East file has firmed. Saudi-led coalition forces confirmed that a Houthi ballistic missile fired at Riyadh at dawn was intercepted and destroyed - the first air-raid alert over the capital since the July escalation - and that attempts against Bisha, Taif, Farasan and Yanbu were thwarted, with no casualties or damage reported. The Houthis claimed missile and drone attacks on sensitive sites in Riyadh and on an Aramco facility at Yanbu. Confirmation without damage resolves the ambiguity the previous hours carried, and resolves it toward containment: the oil-infrastructure channel that would carry a regional strike into index-level risk did not open. CENTCOM's Saturday statement that Hormuz oil and LNG transits reached a six-month high, with more than a billion barrels moved recently, points the same way. Latest-session shared context collected at 21:48Z, partial because its futures and calendar sections were unavailable, shows split internals rather than a trending structure: four of eight megacaps higher with dispersion near 1.5%, semiconductors five of seven higher with Micron up 3.92% against Qualcomm down 5.82%, technology up 0.84% against communication services down 0.74%. That is delayed context rather than live price-path evidence, and it argues against the aligned one-way setup Tail measures. Tail is held at 4, the floor of a closed venue, because no hour in this window offers a mechanism for mean reversion to fail. Stress 24 carries the weekend's headline accumulation into a single reopening auction that falls outside this publication. Confidence rises one point to 73: the evidence is another hour older, but the largest limiter named across the previous four published hours - an unconfirmed strike file - has been resolved by official confirmation and multiple wire reports. The one genuinely observable checkpoint inside the window is Saudi Arabia's Tadawul, which trades on Sundays from roughly 07:00Z and offers the first market-based read on the attacks anywhere. Beyond the window, the Nasdaq-100 quarterly rebalance takes effect at Monday's open with SpaceX's weight confirmed at 2.82% against roughly 1.28% before, and a 24 September Xi visit to Washington is reported but not officially confirmed by Beijing.

lookbackSummary: All 24 preceding hourly assessments were published and every one mapped to green. Tail entered the window at 7 as Friday's post-settlement hours ran down, eased to 6 and then held 5 across the final twenty-two slots. Stress decayed from 28 through 21, where it held for five consecutive hours, then edged back through 22, 23 and 24 into the closing hours. Dominant mode was normal in all 24 hours because no venue was open to produce classifiable structure. Confidence declined steadily from 85 to 72 as distance from the last live tape grew, with the unconfirmed Riyadh and Yanbu strike file repeatedly named as the limiting factor.
outlookSummary: All 24 published slots fall inside the weekend halt: cash closed 20:00Z Friday, the E-mini printed last at 20:59:59Z, and CME equity futures do not reopen until 22:00Z Sunday, one hour after the final slot here. No published hour contains a tradable tape and no scheduled U.S. macro release falls inside the window; the next U.S. catalyst is the Goolsbee speech at 10:30Z Monday and the first high-impact prints are Wednesday's S&P Global flash PMIs. Tail holds 4 through the deepest part of the halt, steps to 5 from 05:00Z, 6 from 10:00Z, 7 from 14:00Z, 8 from 17:00Z and 9 from 19:00Z, reaching 10 in the final hour - a drift that tracks time-to-reopen rather than observed structure. The one genuinely observable checkpoint inside the window is Saudi Arabia's Sunday Tadawul session from roughly 07:00Z, the first market-based read on the Riyadh and Yanbu attacks. Every published hour maps to EA_ON and no danger window is identified.
